title: Traditional forms of Government
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts (to confirm): Buganda (Kabaka, Katikkiro, Lukiiko, appointed chiefs); Nyamwezi (many chiefdoms, each with a Ntemi who inherited the post, advised by elders).

skills.key_step: The child describes how the Buganda kingdom was governed: Kabaka, Katikkiro, Lukiiko and appointed chiefs.

floor.prerequisite: Describes early forms of government in Kenya.
floor.question: Name one Kenyan community that had a king.

steps: Put the Kabaka at the top.

board.do: Draw a pyramid with four levels.

misconceptions.ask: What was the ruler of Buganda called?
misconceptions.repair: Match Buganda with Kabaka and Nyamwezi with Ntemi.
Say the Katikkiro was the Kabaka's main helper.
Write each title with its job on cards.

listen_for: By a vote of all the people
misconceptions.ask: How did a person become Kabaka?
misconceptions.repair: Compare with how a President is chosen today.

checks.question: What was the title of the ruler of Buganda?

skills.key_step: The child describes how the Nyamwezi were governed: many chiefdoms, each with a Ntemi advised by elders.
representations: a map with many small circles
a story of a Ntemi's court

board.do: Write "advised by elders, inherited the post".

listen_for: One large kingdom under one king
misconceptions.ask: How was the Nyamwezi land organised?
misconceptions.repair: Count the chiefdoms on a sketch.

listen_for: By a vote of all the people
misconceptions.ask: How did a person become a Ntemi?
misconceptions.repair: Say the position passed in the royal family.
Act a Ntemi consulting elders before deciding.

misconceptions.ask: In which country do the Nyamwezi live?
misconceptions.repair: Point to central Tanzania on the map.

checks.question: What was the title of a Nyamwezi chief?
Did the Nyamwezi have one big kingdom?

skills.key_step: The child compares Buganda and Nyamwezi government: alike in having a ruler and council, different in size and how chiefs were chosen.
steps: List what only the Nyamwezi had.

board.do: Wait for a ruler and a council.

misconceptions.ask: How did the Buganda system differ from the Nyamwezi?
misconceptions.repair: Say how many rulers each system had.

misconceptions.ask: What did both have in common?
misconceptions.repair: Name the council in each: Lukiiko and council of elders.

misconceptions.ask: Which had many small chiefdoms: Buganda or the Nyamwezi?
misconceptions.repair: Draw one big circle for Buganda and many small ones for the Nyamwezi.

misconceptions.ask: How did Buganda's county chiefs get their posts?

checks.question: Give one similarity between Buganda and Nyamwezi government.
checks.answer: both had a ruler, a council and the ruler judged cases

checks.question: Give one difference.
checks.answer: Buganda was one big kingdom with appointed chiefs; the Nyamwezi had many chiefdoms with inherited Ntemi
